summary: Suggest a soft crafted textile with rounded silhouettes, layered patches and sparse fibers scaled for the view.
objective: The figure still reads at mid-distance and fibers do not conceal eyes, joins or interactive targets.
intent_signals: Create a felt or wool-like appearance
Build a soft textile figure with layered patches
example_prompts: Build a wool-like owl with layered felt wings and an easy-to-read head turn.

principles: Suggest a soft crafted textile with rounded silhouettes, layered patches and sparse fibers scaled for the view.
implementation: Create padded masses, cut felt layers and simple stitched joins; reserve fiber geometry for contours or close focal areas.
Use soft highlights and controlled color variation; light from the side enough to reveal layer thickness without making every fiber compete.
Frame a tactile close view alongside the whole figure; gentle bobbing or jointed puppet movement can fit the intended handmade character.
Build fuzz from 2-4 shell layers offset 0.4-1.2 mm along the normal with 60-70% alpha fibre noise, applied only to silhouette-facing regions and capped at 15% of the figure's surface.
Keep stitched joins at a 2-3 mm pitch and eyes at 8 px or more on screen at the intended size; hold individual fibre strands under 1.5 mm so they never eat a joint or interactive target.
observable_checks: The figure still reads at mid-distance and fibers do not conceal eyes, joins or interactive targets.

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at renderer.toneMappingExposure 1.0; re-tune intensities and fog density under a different tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with stop-motion-inspired timing or toy staging; apparent softness is not a tested cloth or deformation model.

defaults.rationale: Wool has almost no specular lobe, so softness has to come from a sheen-driven fibre rim rather than from geometry density: a dominant HemisphereLight fill at 1.4 with a shallow 1.6:1 key ratio and a bright 10 degree back light lets the fibre edge glow while the body stays matte. Roughness is pinned at 0.9-1.0 with sheen 0.6 / sheenRoughness 0.8 in #ffe6cf, because any clearcoat or gloss immediately reads as plastic rather than textile.

values.value_structure: 30/50/20 dark/mid/light; the fibre rim supplies the lightest values
values.saturation_rule: wool bodies 25-45% saturation; one dyed accent patch up to 70%

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 1.6:1 with a rim at 0.7x key; the soft fill plus bright rim is what makes wool look soft

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: 0.95 body, 0.9 stitched seams; sheen 0.6 with sheenRoughness 0.8 and sheenColor #ffe6cf so the fibre rim lights; no clearcoat and no normal-mapped stitching

motion.ease: sine in-out with a soft settle

values.signature_technique: a sheen-driven fibre rim from a 10 degree back light over a dominant hemisphere fill, so softness comes from the rim rather than from fibre count
never: fibre geometry across the whole figure
normal-mapped stitching instead of modelled seams
